clues: This tiny town has a flat heart, ringed by hills and hard rock. It sits in the north mid part of a green hill state.
Winters here are long, cold, and snowy, with snow staying on the ground for long stretches. Summers are warm and humid.
This town was selected as the state capital in 1805. Its own citizens donated money to build the first state house.
This is the least populous state capital in the United States. It is so small that it has no McDonald's restaurant at all.
The governor of Vermont works in this tiny city. Lawmakers meet in its state house, a short walk from the river.
